comparison: Perfect agreement on experimental design (C1, C128-C131). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support the methodology, though peer reviewers noted limitations regarding absence of certain control groups.

Disagreement on cell type composition changes (C18-C21). OpenEval finds claims supported by Figure 1A-C, but peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting the analysis of non-neuronal cells is 'superficial' and requesting more detailed analysis of glial cell types.
Agreement on ligand-receptor interaction changes (C22-C26). Both OpenEval and peer reviewers support these findings as part of the accepted transcriptomic analysis showing synaptic pathway effects.

Strong agreement on core finding (C27-C29, C2, C115). Both explicitly acknowledge that 17α-estradiol attenuated age-related increases in cellular metabolism and stress while decreasing synaptic activity. Reviewers called this a strength of the study.

Agreement on TF correlation patterns (C30-C32, C33-C37). Both support these transcription factor and gene signature findings as part of the sophisticated analytical approach, though neither extensively critiques the specific methodology.
Agreement on gene signature development (C33-C37, C30-C32). Both support the methodology for identifying unique markers across expression quarters and the inverse correlation between signatures.

Disagreement on non-neuronal cell effects (C38-C39). OpenEval supports neuron-specific effects but notes microglial findings warrant investigation. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, criticizing the 'superficial' analysis of astrocytes and microglia.

Agreement on supervised clustering methodology (C40-C48, C127). Both acknowledge this as a strength, with peer reviewers stating it was 'very helpful in revealing otherwise invisible differences between neuronal groups.'

Partial disagreement on neuron subtype rankings (C49-C55, C56-C57, C113-C114). OpenEval supports findings but notes potential circular reasoning. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating 'the study remains descriptive with no physiological data' to demonstrate functional relevance.

Disagreement on Crh neuron stress phenotype (C56-C64, C58-C65, C112). OpenEval supports the stress phenotype documentation. Peer reviewers initially UNCERTAIN, noting 'the conclusion that CRH neurons are going into senescence is not clearly supported' and requesting 'histological/cellular validation.'

Agreement on uncertainty of HPA axis changes (C65-C66, C125-C126). Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes cortisol elevation non-significant (p=0.078). Peer reviewers did not specifically address aldosterone but requested cellular validation for stress phenotypes.
Agreement on neuron proportion changes (C67-C71). Both support the reciprocal relationship between neuron populations as part of the study's descriptive findings.

Strong agreement on Oxt neuron changes (C73-C78, C69-C70, C81, C84-C85). Both recognize this as a key finding with convergent evidence. Peer reviewers stated 'Oxytocin-expressing neurons seems to be the one most significantly changing' and treated this as a major discovery.

Agreement on TF activity changes (C79-C80, C63, C93). Both support these transcription factor findings as part of mechanistic analysis, though both note associations are speculative and require validation.

Agreement on uncertainty of MR analysis (C81-C85, C82-C83). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to cross-species inference and bidirectional associations. Peer reviewers did not specifically critique MR analysis but focused on direct experimental findings.

Agreement on HPG axis hormone changes (C3-C6, C86-C90, C98). Both support these findings with appropriate statistical testing. Peer reviewers acknowledged '17α-estradiol increased HPG axis activity' as a significant finding.

Strong agreement on testicular pathology uncertainty (C91-C92). Both rate as UNCERTAIN/UNSUPPORTED. OpenEval notes non-significant p=0.15. Peer reviewers criticized 'testes histology which was not properly analyzed and was not even significantly different.'
Agreement on Gnrh1 neuron pathway changes (C93-C94). Both support these findings as part of characterization of neuronal responses to treatment.

Partial agreement on GnRH mediation (C7, C95-C97, C43). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to cross-species MR limitations and overstated causality. Peer reviewers support GnRH as 'one of the key mediators' but did not extensively critique the MR analysis.

Agreement on metabolic effects (C2, C115-C118). Both support the reduction in metabolic pathway expression. OpenEval appropriately qualifies lifespan connection as speculative. Peer reviewers acknowledge metabolic improvements as a core finding.

Partial overlap on metabolic interpretation (C2, C115-C118, C110-C111, C118). OpenEval supports metabolic findings with qualified speculation about lifespan. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, noting lack of functional validation and unclear 'link to 17α-estradiol lifespan extension in rats.'

Agreement on uncertainty of mechanistic claims (C98-C101, C107, C100-C101, C109, C124). Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes mechanism is 'highly speculative and not directly tested.' Peer reviewers state study 'failed to address main weaknesses' and 'insisted in keeping parts not directly linked to findings.'

Partial disagreement on stress signature interpretation (C110-C114, C110-C111, C118). OpenEval supports the interpretive framework as reasonable. Peer reviewers rate as UNCERTAIN, stating 'no physiological data to demonstrate that effects on gene expression is related to metabolic, synaptic or other function.'

Overlap on feeding behavior connection (C113-C114). OpenEval supports connection to feeding behavior via literature. Peer reviewers express concern about lack of physiological validation for functional interpretations.

Agreement on uncertainty of sex differences (C108-C109, C124). Both rate as UNCERTAIN. OpenEval notes claims are 'speculative hypotheses not tested' in male-only study. Peer reviewers state 'Some discussion on sex-specific effects is still required.'

Strong agreement on lifespan extension uncertainty (C108, C14, C16). Peer reviewers explicitly challenged this, stating 'Its not known whether 17α-estradiol leads to lifespan extension in male rats' and authors 'did not add any experimental demonstration.' OpenEval notes lack of direct experimental support.

Agreement on HPA axis stress uncertainty (C125-C126, C66). Both note limitations. OpenEval highlights non-significant cortisol (p=0.078). Peer reviewers did not specifically address but requested cellular validation for stress phenotypes.

Overlap on cortisol/stress interpretation (C125-C126, C65, C112). OpenEval notes non-significant cortisol elevation. Peer reviewers question whether stress phenotype is 'clearly supported by the data' and request validation.

Agreement on supervised clustering methodology (C127). Both support this as a methodological strength that enabled identification of differential responses not possible with unsupervised clustering alone.
